title: Apricot (Jardalu/Khumani): modeled ₹1,744/qtl left, Bhuntar → Palampur
summary: May 2024: reported apricot (Jardalu/Khumani) prices at Bhuntar and Palampur imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 95% of 20 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹1,744 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 2 same-variety market pairs screened for apricot (Jardalu/Khumani) in May 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Palampur report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: May 2024
scenes.caption: Bhuntar (Himachal Pradesh) and Palampur (Himachal Pradesh) both reported apricot (Jardalu/Khumani) prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) on 20 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Bhuntar reported a median ₹6,250 per quintal. Palampur reported a median ₹8,900 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹2,500/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹2,500 per quintal, and Palampur was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 193 km by road
scenes.caption: 193 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~5 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹41/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹1,645 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹1,098 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Palampur report, the rule selects 16 of 20 modeled shipping days. 16 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹1,744 per quintal (₹1,286 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Apricot (Jardalu/Khumani) route from Bhuntar to Palampur was positive on 95% of matched days in May 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹174,400, or ₹128,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to apricot (Jardalu/Khumani)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹41/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Apricot (Jardalu/Khumani) route from Bhuntar to Palampur was positive on 95% of matched days in May 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹174,400, or ₹128,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
